1  NC: 2024:KHC:6591  CRL.P No. 436 of 2024  ORDER

The petitioner is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.PC in Crime No.84/2019 of Surathkal Police Station, pending in S.C.No.112/2021 on the file of the learned VI Additional District Judge, Mangaluru, Dakshina Kannada, registered for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 302, 304-B r/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, on the basis of the first information lodged by Mahammed Nazir.

entities.text: VI Additional District Judge, Mangaluru, Dakshina Kannada
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri Nishit Kumar Shetty, learned counel for the petitioner and Smt. Waheed M.M., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.1.
He is innocent and has not committed any offences as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
He was apprehended on 29.04.2019.
Since then, he is in judicial custody.
Petitioner had earlier filed similar petition in Crl.P.No.3113/2020 which came to be dismissed vide order NC: 2024:KHC:6591 dated 14.09.2020.
Later, he filed Crl.P.No.916/2021 that also came to be dismissed vide order dated 13.08.2021.
While dismissing the said petition, liberty was reserved with the petitioner to move an application for bail after examination of the material witnesses.
A direction was also given to the trial Court to dispose of the case in a time bound manner, at leat within a period of one year.
But thereafter, twice the time for disposal of the case was extended.
Inspite of that, trial in the case is not yet completed.
About 20 witnesses are examined before the trial Court and some of the witnesses including the neighbors have not supported the case of the prosecution.
Under such circumstances, detention of the petitioner would amount to pre trial punishment.
He is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause title to the petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.

Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
5.
Per contra, learned HCGP opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence.
The deceased died within six months from the date of her marriage with the NC: 2024:KHC:6591 petitioner in the matrimonial house in an unnatural way.
After investigation, charge sheet is filed where there are prima-facie materials available against the petitioner.
Considering the nature and seriousness of the offence, the earlier petitions came to be dismissed.
The time extended for conclusion of the trial is not yet completed.
Moreover, all the material witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution.
Under such circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.
Accordingly, she prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is "Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Majeed Ahmad vs State Of Karnataka By on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29263580/
2 Section 439 of Cr.PC?"
My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 7.

sentences.text: Petitioner is arrayed as accused No.1.
He is the husband of the deceased.
The deceased found dead in the house of the petitioner in an unnatural manner within six months from the date of her marriage.
The prosecution has NC: 2024:KHC:6591 collected sufficient materials which prima-facie disclose commission of offence by the petitioner.
Moreover, there is a legal presumption with regard to commission of the offence.
As many as 20 persons are already examined by the trial Court out of 32 witnesses.
The informant and the family members have fully supported the case of the prosecution.
Only the neighbors who were examined as CWs.3 and 4 are not supported the case of the prosecution.
But that cannot be a reason for enlarging the petitioner on bail.
8. When the petitioner had filed Crl.P.No.916/2021, a direction was given to the trial Court to dispose of the matter within a year.
Thereafter, the trial Court sought for extension of time for disposal of the case and on 14.12.2023.
The period was extended by another six months with a direction not to seek for further extension.
The said period of extension is not yet completed.
Moreover, when the material witnesses have fully supported the case of the prosecution.
I do not find any reason to entertain the petition.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in Negative and proceed to pass the following;
NC: 2024:KHC:6591 ORDER Petition is dismissed.
